title: A Queue Built From Two Stacks

concept.title: First in, first out, and how to get it from stacks
body: A **queue** is a line: new items join at the **back** (`enqueue`) and the item that has waited longest leaves from the **front** (`dequeue`): *first in, first out*. A stack gives the opposite order (last in, first out). Two stacks can be combined into a queue, because reversing a stack once reverses the order.

Keep an **inbox** stack and an **outbox** stack. `enqueue` pushes on the inbox. When the front is needed and the outbox is empty, move **all** items from the inbox to the outbox, one by one: the item that came first is now on top of the outbox. Then `dequeue` and `front` use the top of the outbox.

Moving costs time, but every item is moved **at most once**, so a single operation is cheap on average (**amortised O(1)**). You must move only when the outbox is empty; moving earlier would put new items in front of older ones.

statement: Process `n` operations on an initially empty queue. `enqueue x` adds `x` at the back. `dequeue` removes the front item and prints it. `front` prints the front item without removing it. Every line has an operation and a number; for `dequeue` and `front` the number is 0 and must be ignored. The queue is never empty when `dequeue` or `front` is used. Print one line for every `dequeue` and `front`.
inputFormat: Each of the next `n` lines has an operation and a number.
outputFormat: One line for every `dequeue` and `front` operation, in order.
constraints: There is at least one `dequeue` or `front` operation.

examples.input:
6
enqueue 1
enqueue 2
front 0
dequeue 0
enqueue 3
dequeue 0
examples.note: The front is 1; dequeue gives 1; then 2 leaves next.

hints: Use two stacks: an inbox for new items and an outbox for the items that leave.
When the outbox is empty and you need the front, pop everything from the inbox and push it on the outbox.
Never move items while the outbox still has some, or the order would be wrong.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
ops = [input().split() for _ in range(n)]

# Your code here

explanation: New items go on the inbox. When the outbox is empty, the whole inbox is poured into it, which reverses the order so that the oldest item is on top.
solution.complexity: Amortised O(1) per operation, space O(n).
